persona: Everyday customer: home-brewer, gin and wine fan

designs.title: How Beer Is Made
designs.why: As a home-brewer I get it instantly and would wear it to a bottle share: clean, crisp drawings, readable captions, and the hop cone going into the steaming kettle is a nice touch. White on black looks sharp. It does feel a bit like a brewery-tour wall chart, though, and brewers will notice the missing lautering/sparging step and the malting step drawn as a kettle.
designs.fix: Put a proper title ('HOW BEER IS MADE') at the top so it reads as a shirt with a point of view, not a textbook diagram.

designs.title: Gin Botanicals
designs.why: It looks like a nice old botanical plate, and the juniper and coriander are lovely. But nothing on it says gin unless you can read Latin: from across a room it's just 'some plants'. The orange peel reads as an odd snail-shaped blob and the orris is a ruffled thing like a cabbage. Up close the shading is blotchy and crunchy rather than fine engraving.
designs.fix: Add a clear 'GIN' or 'Gin Botanicals' title (or a small G&T glass or still) so a gin fan sees the link at a glance.

designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: It's exactly the Tuscan hillside from a wine trip: farmhouse, cypresses, terraces, grapes up front. I like the mood. But it's packed edge to edge, and up close the texture breaks into broken dotty noise, so on the tee the middle turns into a grey mass. 'VINEYARD.' on its own is generic and a bit flat.
designs.fix: Thin out the busy terraces and foreground with cleaner lines and more white space, so the farmhouse, cypresses and grapes stand out instead of turning grey on the shirt.
